title: Stop the build at a listener with a bad topic

blocks.text: The order platform's message listeners name their broker topic in an annotation, `@Topic("orders.created")`, and the build writes the list of topics the service subscribes to, `practice.generated.Topics`. Last week a listener marked `@Topic("Billing.Refunded")` compiled, shipped, and failed only when the broker refused the subscription in staging.

`TopicProcessor` already writes the list. Finish `check(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/TopicProcessor.java`, which is called for every listener with its topic. When a topic is one the broker refuses (`wellFormed` tells you which), no service may come out of the compile, and the compiler's output must show the developer which listener has the bad topic, by its file and line, and what the topic is. About three lines in total.
The tests compile small listener classes with `javax.tools.JavaCompiler` and your processor, and read what javac reports.

cases.says: listeners with well-formed topics compile, and the generated list holds their topics
a listener with a malformed topic makes the compile fail
the error names the listener's source file and the line of its declaration
javac finishes and reports the bad topic as an error diagnostic, instead of stopping with an exception from the processor

origin.section: An Error Reported at the Element Makes javac Point at the User's Line

concepts: A Messager ERROR passed the element makes javac report the user's file and line and fails the compile; an error left to the generated code points at a file the developer never wrote.
